video_title: 2026-27 Training Camp Media Availability 🎙️ | Dean Wade | 09.30.26

quotes.speaker: Dean Wade
quotes.summary_phrase: Dean Wade on the high basketball IQ of new 76ers teammates
quotes.excerpt: The way they think the game is the most impressive thing.
quotes.quote: It is completely different. You know their tendencies playing against them, but when you are on the same team, you can pick their brain. My biggest thing is the way they think the game is the most impressive thing. Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown, everyone, the way they think the game is at such a high level. As an NBA player, you think you know the game well, and then you get on a team like this and it is night and day. You see the way they think about plays, think about defenses, the way they think about rotations. It is similar to some things I thought, but they go a little more in-depth and it is super impressive.
quotes.social_post: Dean Wade says the basketball IQ of his new 76ers teammates is eye opening. He notes that watching Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, and Jaylen Brown think the game is at a totally different level than what he experienced previously.

quotes.speaker: Dean Wade
quotes.summary_phrase: Dean Wade on being encouraged to shoot more by his coaches
quotes.excerpt: You will never be more open than open, and so you just have to shoot the ball.
quotes.quote: I have been told that a lot in my career. You will never be more open than open, and so you just have to shoot the ball. Sometimes I try to think the play, think the defense is going to rotate and they do not. That is the biggest thing. I have to shoot the ball, I have to be open. That is what they need me to do is to shoot the ball when I am open and play defense. I am sure he has been on me a few times already, but it is better to be told to shoot it than to stop shooting.
quotes.social_post: Dean Wade says the coaching staff is pushing him to be more aggressive with his shot. He admits he sometimes overthinks the defense, but knows his role is to shoot the ball whenever he is open.

quotes.speaker: Dean Wade
quotes.summary_phrase: Dean Wade on the versatility of the 76ers roster
quotes.excerpt: We have so many versatile defenders, athletes. We have so many good players that can do different things.
quotes.quote: It is crazy. We have so many vets on this team who have seen so many different things and played completely different styles of basketball. I am interested to see what we stick to or what we try. It is pretty impressive we have so many versatile defenders, athletes. We have so many good players that can do different things. I think we can really go pretty deep inside the defensive playbook and rotations and do different things that other teams do not have the ability to do. That is what is going to separate us on the defensive end.
quotes.social_post: Dean Wade believes the defensive versatility of the 76ers roster will be their biggest separator this season. He says the team has the personnel to go deep into the defensive playbook and run schemes other teams cannot.

quotes.speaker: Dean Wade
quotes.summary_phrase: Dean Wade on the 76ers' transition offense potential
quotes.excerpt: We have so many great players, so many unstoppable people in transition.
quotes.quote: We have so many great players, so many unstoppable people in transition. It is almost like a free throw or basket in transition. I think a big emphasis is getting out more in transition. The way our defense is, how many turnovers we can create, we should be unbelievable in transition. Especially with Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey, all those guys, they get out in transition, those are hard people to stop. When you are out in transition, it makes everything a little bit easier. Your decision-making can be easier, you are going to see the open guy a little easier.
quotes.social_post: The 76ers are prioritizing transition offense this year. Dean Wade says with players like Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey, the team should be unbelievable in the open floor.

quotes.speaker: Dean Wade
quotes.summary_phrase: Dean Wade on the decision-making of Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown
quotes.excerpt: They never make the wrong decision, they are always making the right decision.
quotes.quote: They are unbelievable. They are so fast and quick. Tyrese Maxey, he gets out in transition and it is unbelievable how fast he moves, how fast he can change direction. I feel like the thing that really surprised me the most is they never make the wrong decision, they are always making the right decision. If that is dashing it out on the baseline, kicking out, scoring, whatever it is, they always make the right decision. That is hard, especially for a young guy. Tyrese Maxey is only in his second year, so seeing him, he is playing like he is a vet. He knows the right plays and he is doing it and he is not forcing anything.
quotes.social_post: Dean Wade is impressed by the maturity of Tyrese Maxey. He says Maxey plays like a veteran and rarely makes the wrong decision in transition, whether that means scoring or finding an open teammate.

quotes.speaker: Dean Wade
quotes.summary_phrase: Dean Wade on his relationship with Mike Gansey
quotes.excerpt: He is no different than what he was when I was in Cleveland.
quotes.quote: I will not lie, it has not really changed our relationship. We still talk trash about our colleges and when we play each other and all the sports things. He is no different than what he was when I was in Cleveland. He is always checking in, seeing how my family is, I ask how his family is and he genuinely cares. So that is nice to see, but the change in title and everything has not changed him as a person. Seeing him as the top dog is always fun.
quotes.social_post: Dean Wade says his relationship with Mike Gansey remains unchanged despite Gansey's rise to the top of the front office. He says Gansey is still the same person he knew in Cleveland.

quotes.speaker: Dean Wade
quotes.summary_phrase: Dean Wade on his defensive alignment with Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey
quotes.excerpt: The way they think the game is similar to the way I think the game.
quotes.quote: There is a lot. The past few days, especially with Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey, the way they think the game is similar to the way I think the game, especially on the defensive end. When I get out on the same team as those guys, it is always something I kind of like to pick their brain. They have a thought, have a half-thought, very similar to the way I thought the game. When I see early, the past couple weeks, with Tyrese Maxey and those guys, I love the way he plays. I really do. Any time I get out there on his team, I love it because he is flying around in transition, he is making the right cuts, he is sacrificing shots.
quotes.social_post: Dean Wade says he loves playing alongside Tyrese Maxey because of his high defensive IQ and willingness to sacrifice shots. He notes that their defensive instincts are very similar.

quotes.speaker: Dean Wade
quotes.summary_phrase: Dean Wade on his defensive development and coaching influences
quotes.excerpt: Not every team has a defender. You need to like, move good enough laterally.
quotes.quote: I think a little bit of both. Kansas State when I was there, I think we were like a top-five defensive team in the nation and we played the same way we switched everything. I had to learn that pretty fast when I was at Kansas State. I was not really diving into my defensive ability then too much. I just did it good enough to get stops. In the NBA, it was a way to stick in the league. I was a two-way, I was undrafted. I had to figure out a way to kind of separate myself. I had great coaches when I was young in the NBA, a guy named Josh Broghammer and Chris Darnell were my coaches and they were counting on me. We sat down one time and they were like, if you want to stay in this league, every team has a scorer and a shooter, every team has somebody that can create. Not every team has a defender. You need to move good enough laterally, that is where you can stick if you want to stick in this league. So I took that conversation and I dove in headfirst into that.
quotes.social_post: Dean Wade reflects on his path to the NBA, noting that he had to commit to being a defender to stick in the league. He credits early coaching for teaching him that defensive versatility is the key to longevity.
